authority.archive: SalesJobRuntimeService owns a private WeakMap of currently executing actual transaction executors bound to its live archive scheduler lease, orderId, archiveBatchId and cutoffMs. Only its actual archive coordinator callback enters/exits this scope with try/finally. The fulfillmentArchive adapter resolves the real salesJobs singleton and injects a fixed read-only authorization callback to the participant; callback verifies the same tx object and exact scope/live principal. No token/role/identity from command can grant authority. No publicly callable grant/register method or exported bearer token.
authority.transaction: Archive methods require both tx.query function and successful trusted authorization callback with same tx; reject absent/out-of-scope executor. Provider never BEGIN/COMMIT/acquire another connection. Lifecycle/transaction-aware OpenMatter requires the actual caller executor verified against the database service current request-context databaseTransaction; native fixtures use the real withTransaction executor/context, not a fabricated query object.
authority.lockPrerequisite: Caller acquires Sales root/lines/mappings first; provider never acquires Sales locks in reverse. prepare locks owner roots/children by ascending IDs, verifies closed state and returns real observed hashes. archive rechecks same locked state/expected manifest, then copy/readback/delete. All holds remain in caller transaction.
authority.schedulerContext: SalesJobRuntimeService adds the existing context service dependency and enters context.storage.run with a controlled async job scope (databaseTransaction:null, current job signal/deadline/startedAt, no claimed human auth) before database.withTransaction. The actual MySqlDatabaseService then binds the actual transaction object in that scope; provider checks equality. No framework modification. Non-transactional OpenMatter getOrderArchiveStatus similarly establishes its own controlled read context before its own read transaction if no current context exists; the transaction-aware sibling never opens another transaction/context/connection.

hashAlgorithm.row: SHA256 UTF-8 JSON.stringify(array of [columnName,normalizedValue] pairs in exact canonical owner schema column order). Include original id and generated business values; exclude archive_batch_id/archived_at/row_hash only.
hashAlgorithm.canonicalColumns: Explicit immutable arrays in server/src/modules/fulfillment/fulfillmentArchiveSchema.js, reviewed against every field of owner Design4.3-4.15. Full native column/constraint parity is required; no SELECT-star-derived runtime order.
hashAlgorithm.normalization: NULL stays null; BIGINT/INT/boolean identities and quantities canonical decimal strings without leading zero (zero allowed quantities), DECIMAL uses declared scale without floating-point conversion, DATE is YYYY-MM-DD, text is exact UTF-8, JSON recursively sorts object keys preserving array order and values and rejects non-finite/unsafe numeric values. No implicit locale/date-time conversion.
hashAlgorithm.table: SHA256 of ascending numeric original-id rows joined as id:row_hash followed by LF for each row; empty table SHA256 of empty bytes. No archive metadata in row digest. All12 tableCounts/hashSummary keys required even when zero.

failureSemantics.badShapeOrType: TypeError before query/mutation; exact allowed keys and safe bounds; no coercion
failureSemantics.openOrUnknown: OpenMatter returns strict OPEN/UNKNOWN safe result; participant throws FULFILLMENT_ARCHIVE_NOT_ELIGIBLE (no writes) and caller rolls back
failureSemantics.manifestOrExistingRowMismatch: ARCHIVE_DATA_CONFLICT; no overwrite/update of immutable archive rows; caller rolls back all Sales/owner effects
failureSemantics.technicalFailure: Propagate safe dependency failure to coordinator; no swallowing into success; actual whole transaction rollback or durable unknown-commit recovery
failureSemantics.replay: Same order/batch/complete original12 table counts/hashes and persistent routing/manifest must prove same effect. No active rows plus complete matching archive yields REPLAYED. Existing same-ID rows may only be reused after exact same batch/hash and complete manifest validation; partial/different evidence never implies success. Different batch/hash is conflict, not repair.
